html:
SMTO-CTX-0031 — A saved result is too big to show the AI model in one piece

GUID: 4af192db-59d7-513a-9e51-f984417be3a5
Slug: result-read-exceeds-model-budget
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: stored-result-recovery

What happened

  • The task asked to look at part of a saved result, such as a command's output, but that part was too large for the AI model's remaining space. The saved result is still there, and nothing was run again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep going and watch its activity for a smaller read of the same result. SMTO gives the task an exact smaller read to use next, so it can continue on its own.
  2. If the task keeps asking for the same large piece, select Steer and tell it to read that result in smaller parts. Reading in smaller parts fits the model's space without losing any of the saved output.
  3. Don't ask the task to run the original command again just to see its output. The output is already saved, and running the command again could repeat its changes.

What success looks like

  • The task's activity shows it reading the saved result in parts and moving on.

If it still fails

  • If the task stops on this message, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't take this message as a sign that the original command failed; it only means the piece was too big to show.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • read_result for a Task Context alias was rejected by model-input admission because the requested receipt page does not fit the run's remaining input budget; no text was returned and a smaller read of the same receipt and offset was offered.

What this means

  • For a resolved notebook alias, the page is checked against the run's model-input budget. Rejection returns zero characters and a smaller read_result action pinned to the same canonical receipt and offset. It does not discard the stored receipt or reexecute its operation.

Why this can happen

  • For a resolved notebook alias, the page is checked against the run's model-input budget. Rejection returns zero characters and a smaller read_result action pinned to the same canonical receipt and offset. It does not discard the stored receipt or reexecute its operation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the returned next_action, canonical reference, offset and reduced character limit.

How to fix it

  • Follow the returned next_action: a smaller read_result on the same canonical receipt and offset. A budget rejection says nothing about whether the original operation succeeded; do not rerun it to recover output. Note that finish_page documents a known gap where a real alias overflow may raise KeyError in context_reads instead of returning the smaller-page action.
  • Follow the supplied smaller read_result action for the same receipt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Retry only the supplied smaller receipt read; the originating operation is not retried.

How to verify the fix

  • A smaller exact page is returned with its original receipt identity and paging information.

What not to do

  • Do not rerun the original command to retrieve its output or infer that budget rejection means it failed.

Technical notes

  • The rejected read returns no page text and executes no originating command.
  • A read-budget rejection does not establish whether the originating operation succeeded.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
